question: to the Commission Asger Christensen (Renew) Subject:

The Commission has shared with Member States draft marketing standards for cider and perry as secondary legislation to the regulation establishing a common organisation of the markets in agricultural products (Regulation (EU) No 1308/2013). The current draft of the marketing standards would have a major impact on long-standing Nordic ciders. It would re-classify them so that they could only be called ‘cider-based’ drinks, despite their long tradition and significant share of the European cider market. There is no precedent for such a standard, no equivalent rules for soft drinks or beer, and no evidence of consumer demand. Further, the draft offers no consumer benefit, adds regulatory burden and costs, and runs counter to the EU’s simplification and competitiveness agenda. It would downgrade Nordic-style ciders compared to other European styles. In light of this: 1.
Does the Commission consider the proposal to be aligned with the EU’s simplification and competitiveness agenda?
Does the Commission consider that the proposal will provide added value to the sector?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (2.6.2026) In its reply to question P-001116/2026, the Commission explained how it has been discussing different possible approaches for the establishment of marketing standards for cider and perry with national experts and representatives of the sector since 2024, after having published a report1 and an impact assessment2 on marketing standards including those for cider and perry in 2023. With the support of a large majority of Member States and of representatives of the sector, the Commission will pursue discussions with all Member States to further explore options with the objective of covering all products currently present on the market under the name of cider, in full respect of EU diversity and of providing added value to the EU cider sector as a whole, contributing to the EU competitiveness agenda, as marketing standards would equally benefit apple and pear growers as well as cider and perry producers. While the non-paper circulated up to now in different revised versions, it is not yet final and remains open to improvement, the standard envisaged by the Commission aims to harmonise rules across the whole EU market without applying to EU exports or requiring any reformulation of cider products and perry products, although some of them may need to be labelled in a way that ensure that consumers are accurately informed about the type of product they purchase and consume.
